_citation: Stilck França, García-Patrón. 'Limitations of optimization algorithms on noisy quantum devices.' Nature Physics 17, 1221–1227 (2021).
_methodology: Proves via relative-entropy bounds and mirror descent that for any noisy quantum circuit solving a cost-function or sampling problem, the product p×L (per-gate error × circuit depth) upper-bounds achievable approximation quality. If p×L > ~1, output converges to the noise fixed point (mixed state) and is indistinguishable from random sampling. Applies to ANY non-fault-tolerant noisy circuit — variational (QAOA, VQE, QML), quantum annealing, AND non-variational optimization/estimation (QAE, Grover, quantum walk). Does not apply to fault-tolerant error-corrected circuits.
_audit_2026_04_20: Applicable-families list broadened beyond variational. Per the paper's general scope (any noisy non-FT circuit optimizing a cost function), amplitude-estimation, Grover, and quantum-walk are now in scope. Excluding them previously hid the bound from ~228 finance experiments (audit fix M1).

noise_bound.formula: If p * L > c (for constant c ≈ 1), then cost function expectation converges to the trivial (random) value exponentially fast. p = single-gate error rate, L = circuit depth.
noise_bound.interpretation: p * L > 1 means the noise has corrupted the circuit beyond any useful signal. Even p * L ≈ 0.1-1.0 severely limits the approximation quality.
noise_bound.practical_threshold_note: Below p*L = 0.1 there may be some useful signal; above, advantage is impossible.

fault_tolerant.label: Error-corrected logical gates
fault_tolerant.note: Stilck França bound is irrelevant for FT circuits — this framework only constrains NISQ.

_verdict_rules._guidance: Only runs on variational/NISQ algorithms. If algorithm is QAOA/VQE/QA and noise_model.is_noisy = true (or inferred from hardware name): compute p*L and compare against threshold. If p*L > 1 → fails. If 0.1 < p*L ≤ 1 → conditional. If p*L ≤ 0.1 → potentially_viable. If no noise info → insufficient_data. If algorithm is not variational → not_applicable.
